record.original_question: Characterize the extreme rays of DNN_n, the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices that are both positive semidefinite and entrywise nonnegative. A matrix A in a convex cone K generates an extreme ray when every decomposition A = B + C with B and C in K forces B and C to be scalar multiples of A.

evidence.quote: The extreme rays of the doubly nonnegative cone DN N n are not fully understood.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{DNN}_n$ denote the cone of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices that are simultaneously positive semidefinite and entrywise nonnegative (the doubly nonnegative cone). Recall that $\mathrm{DNN}_n$ is a closed convex cone in the space of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices. A nonzero matrix $A$ in a convex cone $K$ is said to generate an extreme ray of $K$ if, whenever $A = B + C$ with $B, C \in K$, both $B$ and $C$ are nonnegative scalar multiples of $A$.

Give a complete characterization of the extreme rays of $\mathrm{DNN}_n$ for every integer $n \geq 2$: that is, describe explicitly (in terms of structural, combinatorial, or algebraic properties of $A$, such as rank, support pattern, or factorization $A = XX^\top$) precisely which matrices $A \in \mathrm{DNN}_n$ generate extreme rays.
artifact.status_search_result: A general characterization of the extreme rays of $\mathrm{DNN}_n$ for arbitrary $n$ remains open. Partial results are known: rank-one nonnegative matrices always generate extreme rays, and a complete classification has been obtained for small cases — notably for $n = 5$, where extreme rays of $\mathrm{DNN}_5$ are exactly rank-one nonnegative matrices or slack matrices of certain irreducible self-dual cones over a pentagon (Gouveia–Pong–Sosa, 2022). New families of extreme rays continue to be discovered, indicating that no full general characterization is currently available.

status_evidence.title: Self-Dual Polyhedral Cones and Their Slack Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: If the underlying cone is irreducible, then the corresponding PSD slacks are not only DNN matrices but are extreme rays of the cone of DNN matrices, corresponding to a family of extreme rays not previously described.
status_evidence.claim: New families of extreme rays of the DNN cone continue to be identified, indicating no complete characterization is yet available.

status_evidence.title: Generalizations of doubly nonnegative cones and their comparison
status_evidence.snippet: Studies generalizations of the doubly nonnegative cone and structural properties.
status_evidence.claim: Research on the structure of DNN cones is ongoing.

status_evidence.title: The difference between 5×5 doubly nonnegative and completely positive matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of structure of 5x5 DNN matrices versus completely positive matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Structural results are known for small n but not in general.
